project.name: pjproject / pjsip
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged ARVO checkout at `950081c737063e12aa95cc4a7b332b85ae6a8d5d`, an earlier still-vulnerable pjproject snapshot whose line map matches the cited statements below. The metadata `vulnerable_commit` is the later commit `214d6bc7d4b9c7f4af935bbf8d68099c83c5dee2`; both snapshots still contain the commented-out length check in `compare_handler`, and the staged `patch.diff` restores that exact check.

staged_source_snapshot.description: All file and line anchors below were resolved against the staged ARVO workspace checkout used by Stage 01 reproduction. It still contains the vulnerable `compare_handler` implementation and the `Supported` short-name registration that make the saved hash-collision path possible.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value; Crash State: find_handler / int_parse_msg / pjsip_parse_msg; Sanitizer: memory (MSAN).
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `__interceptor_memcmp`, with project stack `compare_handler -> find_handler_imp -> find_handler -> int_parse_msg -> pjsip_parse_msg`. The exact staged witness is the 19-byte ASCII buffer `SIP/2.0415\nTON+Vip:` (`53 49 50 2f 32 2e 30 34 31 35 0a 54 4f 4e 2b 56 69 70 3a`). `int_parse_status_line` accepts the prefix `SIP/2.0415\n` as a SIP response status line, and `int_parse_msg` then tokenizes the header name `TON+Vip` with `hname.slen == 7`. `find_handler` hashes that exact-case token with `pj_hash_calc` to `107`; static inspection of the registered parser names in the staged source shows the only existing handler record with hash `107` is the one-byte short header `k` registered for `Supported`. During parser initialization, `int_register_parser("k", ...)` stack-allocates `handler_rec rec`, copies only `'k'` and its NUL terminator into `rec.hname`, computes the same hash `107`, and then copies the whole struct into the global `handler[]` table, leaving the remaining bytes of `handler[pos].hname` uninitialized. In vulnerable `compare_handler`, the length comparison block is commented out, so once the hash matches the 1-byte stored name and 7-byte attacker name fall through to `pj_memcmp(r1->hname, name, name_len)`. `memcmp` therefore reads seven bytes from the partially initialized stored handler name and MemorySanitizer reports `Uninitialized bytes in MemcmpInterceptorCommon at offset 2 inside [.., 7)`. The staged patch resolves this exact path by restoring the `r1->hname_len` vs `name_len` checks so mismatched-length hash collisions return before `pj_memcmp`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled header name token used by the vulnerable handler lookup.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the 19-byte buffer `53 49 50 2f 32 2e 30 34 31 35 0a 54 4f 4e 2b 56 69 70 3a`, i.e. ASCII `SIP/2.0415\nTON+Vip:`. After `int_parse_status_line` consumes the `SIP/2.0415\n` prefix, this statement reads the next token `TON+Vip` immediately before the trailing colon, so `hname.slen == 7` and `hname.ptr` points at those seven attacker-controlled bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer origin for the uninitialized bytes later read by `pj_memcmp`. `rec` is stack-allocated here before its `hname` array is only partially initialized and then copied wholesale into the global handler table.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved MSan trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `rec` in the stack frame of `int_register_parser` at line 611; the exact `handler_rec rec;` declaration in the staged checkout is line 613.
tainted_value_origin.note: These bytes are not attacker-controlled; the attacker-controlled header token only selects the colliding lookup path and the overlong compare length that exposes them.

root_cause.description: Missing length guard. After a hash match, `compare_handler` does not reject mismatched name lengths, so the one-byte stored shortname `k` and the seven-byte attacker token `TON+Vip` fall through to `pj_memcmp`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch removes this comment block and reinstates the two `r1->hname_len` vs `name_len` checks, which is exactly the obligation missing on the crashing path.

sink.description: MSAN sink. `pj_memcmp` is invoked with `name_len == 7` on the stored one-byte handler name buffer, so the compare reads the uninitialized tail copied from `int_register_parser`'s stack `rec`.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in MemcmpInterceptorCommon at offset 2 inside [0x..., 7)` and the first project frame at `compare_handler /src/pjsip/pjsip/src/pjsip/sip_parser.c:605:12`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness prefix `SIP/2.0415\n` is accepted here as a SIP response status line, so `int_parse_msg` enters the header-parsing loop that later tokenizes `TON+Vip` and reaches the vulnerable handler lookup.

evidence_limitations: The staged vulnerable checkout reproduced by Stage 01 is commit `950081c737063e12aa95cc4a7b332b85ae6a8d5d`, not the later metadata `vulnerable_commit`; all line anchors above therefore refer to the staged tree that actually produced the saved crash trace.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 relied only on the staged source, patch, saved PoC, and saved MemorySanitizer trace. That was sufficient to close the chain without adding instrumentation.

coarse_trace.summary: Parser initialization registers the `Supported` short header `k`; `int_register_parser` partially initializes a stack `handler_rec` for that one-byte name and copies the whole struct, including the uninitialized tail of `hname`, into the global `handler[]` table.

The exact witness is admitted as SIP response `SIP/2.0 415`, `int_parse_msg` tokenizes header name `TON+Vip`, and exact-case `find_handler` hashes it to 107, colliding with the stored `k` short-header record.

Once the hash matches, the vulnerable code skips any `hname_len` comparison because the length-check block is commented out, so the one-byte stored name and seven-byte attacker name fall through to bytewise comparison.
`pj_memcmp` compares seven bytes from the stored `k` handler name against `TON+Vip`, reads the handler record's uninitialized tail, and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

fine_trace.note: MSAN origin. While `init_parser` registers the `Supported` short name `k`, `int_register_parser` stack-allocates temporary `handler_rec rec`. The saved trace names this stack frame as the origin of the later uninitialized bytes.

For this short-name registration, `name == "k"`, so `rec.hname_len == 1`, `rec.hname_hash == 107`, and only `rec.hname[0] = 'k'` plus `rec.hname[1] = '\0'` are initialized. Bytes `rec.hname[2..]` remain uninitialized on the stack.

The whole temporary record is copied into the global handler table, so the stored short-header entry for `k` carries the same uninitialized `hname` tail. The saved MSAN trace reports this `pj_memcpy` as the store that moved the poisoned bytes into memory later read by `pj_memcmp`.

Source. After the exact witness prefix `SIP/2.0415\n` is parsed as a status line, the header loop reads the next token `TON+Vip`. This gives `hname.ptr` the attacker-controlled header-name bytes and sets `hname.slen == 7` before the trailing colon check.

fine_trace.code:
hash = pj_hash_calc(0, hname->ptr, (unsigned)hname->slen);
func = find_handler_imp(hash, hname);
fine_trace.note: Exact-case lookup hashes `TON+Vip` to `107` and immediately enters `find_handler_imp`. In the staged source, the only registered handler name with hash `107` is the one-byte shortname `k` from step 2, so this exact-case search reaches `compare_handler` on that stored record before any lowercase fallback.

Root cause. Once the colliding hashes match, `compare_handler` does not reject the one-byte stored name and the seven-byte attacker token on length. The staged patch restores exactly these checks so the collision returns before any bytewise read of `r1->hname` beyond its initialized prefix.

Sink. `pj_memcmp` compares seven bytes from the stored `k\0...` handler-name buffer against `TON+Vip`. Because step 2 only initialized the first two bytes of that stored name, the compare reads the uninitialized tail and MemorySanitizer reports `Uninitialized bytes in MemcmpInterceptorCommon at offset 2 inside [0x..., 7)`.

allocation_context.note: The saved origin frame is the function line `int_register_parser /src/pjsip/pjsip/src/pjsip/sip_parser.c:611`; the exact `handler_rec rec;` declaration in the staged checkout is line 613.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MSAN report's first project frame is `compare_handler` at `pjsip/src/pjsip/sip_parser.c:605`, which is the exact fine-trace sink.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes, in the combined sense needed for this bug. MemorySanitizer names stack allocation of `rec` in `int_register_parser` as the byte origin, step 2 shows those bytes are preserved by whole-struct copy into `handler[pos]`, and the staged patch fixes the separate missing length check in `compare_handler` that lets that stored tail reach `pj_memcmp`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `compare_handler -> find_handler_imp -> find_handler -> int_parse_msg -> pjsip_parse_msg`; the fine trace fills in the preceding handler-registration and hash-collision steps inside the same staged source file.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 0 allocates `rec`, step 1 leaves `rec.hname[2..]` uninitialized while hashing shortname `k`, step 2 copies that tail into the global handler record, and step 6 passes the same stored buffer to `pj_memcmp` with attacker-controlled `name_len == 7`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch removes the commented-out length block in `compare_handler` and restores the two `r1->hname_len` vs `name_len` checks, so the `k`/`TON+Vip` hash-collision path returns before `pj_memcmp` can read the stored handler record's uninitialized tail.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` is exactly the 19-byte buffer `53 49 50 2f 32 2e 30 34 31 35 0a 54 4f 4e 2b 56 69 70 3a`, i.e. ASCII `SIP/2.0415\nTON+Vip:`. Stage 01's saved run reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `compare_handler` / `pj_memcmp` when `fuzz-sip` processes that exact input.

format.name: 19-byte raw SIP response fragment for fuzz-sip
format.contract: An exact 19-byte input equal to ASCII `SIP/2.0415\nTON+Vip:`. In the staged parser, the prefix `SIP/2.0415\n` must remain a valid response status line, and the following header token before the trailing colon must remain exact-case `TON+Vip` so that `pj_hash_calc` yields 107, collides with the registered short header `k`, and reaches the vulnerable missing-length-check path in `compare_handler`. The staged artifacts prove this exact witness only; they do not prove a broader family of hash-colliding header names.
